name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with a seat, operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less, in one of three classes: Class I pedal assist to 20 mph, Class II throttle to 20 mph, and Class III pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-9 and regulated by §§32-20B-10 to 32-20B-15.
restrictions: A bicycle or tricycle with a seat or saddle, operable pedals, and an electric motor of 750 watts or less
Class I assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 20 mph
Class II can be propelled by its motor without pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph
Class III assists only while the rider pedals, stops assisting at 28 mph, and must have a working speedometer
The motor must disengage or stop when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who modifies its speed or propulsion must update the label
Class III riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class III riders under 18 and all Class III passengers must wear a bicycle helmet; no statewide helmet rule for Class I or II
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, title or registration
Class I and Class II may ride on any bicycle or multi-use path unless the governing entity prohibits it
Class III is kept off bicycle and multi-use paths unless the path runs within or beside a roadway or the governing entity allows it
Class III may ride a nonmotorized natural-surface trail unless the managing entity prohibits or restricts it
Only Class I is allowed on the George S. Mickelson Trail, since SB 79 (2025)
